predecessors.text: the south-western borderlands of Bornu between Cliopatria's 1808 and 1809 shapes, as in the empire-of-kanem dossier

ledger.x: 21 February 1804: the Sokoto jihad begins.
21 February 1804: 'Yunfa declared war on dan Fodio'.
1805: the jihadists take Kebbi.
1807: Katsina and Daura fall.
1807: Kano falls.
c. 1808: Nupe falls. 'The kingdom fell to the Sokoto forces c. 1808' and Mallam Dendo was installed as emir of Bida.
1808: the jihad reaches Bornu.
3 October 1808: Alkalawa falls and Gobir with it.
October 1808: the war with Gobir ends with the fall of Alkalawa.
1809: Bello makes Sokoto a city.
1809: the Bornu borderlands pass to the caliphate in Cliopatria's shapes.
1809: Hausaland and the Benue lands complete Cliopatria's outline.
ledger.cp: Hausa kingdoms of Zamfara and Zazzau, and the Jukun, Bauchi, Gombe and Adamawa lands

ledger.x: 1824: Ilorin is an emirate of the caliphate.
Later 1820s: the Fulani are driven out of Bornu; the Sokoto page gives no end to the Bornu war (it records Bello's debates with al-Kanemi undated), so 1827 is the empire-of-kanem dossier's bridge.
1834: the western and southern strips complete the caliphate's greatest outline.
ledger.cp: Gurma, Liptako and the lands between (no dossier)

ledger.x: 1836: Ilorin's forces burn Oyo-Ile.
1840: the old Oyo core drops out of the caliphate's outline.
1901: the British move into the caliphate.
13 March 1903: the Vizier concedes.
[Review af-03-b: confidence 3 to 2, because the page divides the land between the British, French and Germans while this event gives all of it to british-africa.].

wars.name: Fulani War
wars.outcome: Sokoto victory: Kebbi 1805, Katsina and Kano 1807, Gobir's capital Alkalawa 1808 (Yunfa killed); Sokoto becomes the capital in 1809.

wars.name: Sokoto-Bornu war
wars.outcome: In 1808 the jihadists burn Ngazargamu but only partly succeeded; Muhammad al-Kanemi leads Bornu's resistance.

wars.name: Kebbawa resistance (Argungu)
wars.outcome: A combined Sokoto-Gwandu force besieged Argungu in 1831; peace 1831-1849; in 1849 the Kebbawa leader 'renounced his allegiance to the Caliphate and adopted the title of Sarkin Kebbi'; a peace treaty in 1868 ended the hostilities.

wars.name: Gobir revolt of 1836
wars.outcome: 'A serious revolt occurred in 1836 in the city-state of Gobir, which was crushed by Muhammed Bello at the Battle of Gawakuke.'

wars.name: Ilorin-Oyo war
wars.outcome: Ilorin, an emirate under Gwandu, burns Oyo-Ile and pushes south until 'Ilorin's southward expansion effectively ended in 1838' (the Battle of Osogbo).

wars.name: British conquest of the Sokoto Caliphate
wars.outcome: The British enter in 1901, take Gwandu (12 March) and Sokoto (13 March 1903); Attahiru I is beaten in June and killed; Burmi is 27 July 1903.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes a Sokoto frontier before the colonial partition; the Hausa heartland is known by emirate, the Sahelian, Benue and Yoruba edges are approximate.
